results.title: Andrés Rodríguez-Pose's Post - LinkedIn
results.content: #Investment returns depend less on the volume of capital than on a region’s institutional “chemistry.” We use a latent-class approach —that allows “returns” to vary by place— across 230 EU regions to show that the efficacy of physical capital and #innovation is, in practice, hostage to the quality of local #governments. The same types of spending can generate very different growth outcomes depending on whether public authority is predictable, impartial, and competent (or instead erratic, politicised, and slow). By contrast, in #regions where local #institutions create a labyrinth for economic activity, the strongest catalyst for growth is often not a grand #infrastructure project, but quieter investment in human capital: #education and skills. Better government, higher trust, and lower corruption don’t just boost growth; they also narrow the gap between #Europe’s winners and laggards by making policy work more evenly across the #EU. results.title: Europe's Development Trap: Regions Stuck in Economic Winter
results.content: # Europe's Development Trap: Regions Stuck in Economic Winter. While the struggle to find a decent panettone may feel like a crisis of the highest order, Pierre-Alexandre Balland and Ron Boschma identify a far more enduring stalemate in their latest —and profoundly interesting— Regional Studies Journal article: the structural inability of #regions to develop new complex activities. Not bad for a country in which most of the regions seem stuck in a structural trap (according to this analysis). The complexity loop seems to correlate (from memory) with regions that have higher rates of new, endogenous business formation. The UK in particular has been really bad at understanding this link and has some of the lowest rates of new entrepreneur-employers (people who start a company that hires employees) outside of the SE. And, sadly, the single strongest indicator of a new business’s success is whether the founders have close personal relationships with other entrepreneur-employers, so it is a self-reinforcing feedback loop.
